messages.subject: Networking confusion and inexperience
parts:
I had my shiny-server running great but I restarted my computer (ubuntu 12.04, 64 bit) and now it won't connect.  I get the following response

$shiny-server
[2014-07-21 20:37:43.530] [INFO] shiny-server - Shiny Server v1.0.0.42 (Node.js v0.10.21)
[2014-07-21 20:37:43.533] [INFO] shiny-server - Using config file "/opt/shiny-server/config/
default.config"
[2014-07-21 20:37:43.575] [INFO] shiny-server - Starting listener on 0.0.0.0:3838
[2014-07-21 20:37:43.580] [ERROR] shiny-server - HTTP server error (0.0.0.0:3838): listen EADDRINUSE
[2014-07-21 20:37:43.580] [INFO] shiny-server - Shutting down worker processes


I have a DIR-810L D-Link router that I have set up to forward UDP port 3838 like before.  Under Advanced and Port Forwarding I've tried changing the IP required from the internal to the external and back to the internal address. This is what I believe I had to do last time to get web traffic to the apps.

I have the current version of shiny-server and did the ubuntu auto-update and restarted. 

My default.config is in opt/shiny-server/config and is the same file that comes with the install forwarding to 3838.

# Instruct Shiny Server to run applications as the user "shiny"
run_as shiny;

# Define a server that listens on port 3838
server {
  listen 3838;

  # Define a location at the base URL
  location / {

    # Host the directory of Shiny Apps stored in this directory
    site_dir /srv/shiny-server;

    # Log all Shiny output to files in this directory
    log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;

    # When a user visits the base URL rather than a particular application,
    # an index of the applications available in this directory will be shown.
    directory_index on;
  }
}

What am I missing to evaluate is going wrong?
